title: All Paths from Source to Target
statement:
# All Paths from Source to Target

A directed acyclic graph with `n` nodes is given as an adjacency list `graph`, where `graph[i]` lists the neighbours of node `i` in ascending order and every edge points from a smaller node to a larger one.

Enumerate every directed path from node `0` to node `n - 1`. Each path is written as the sequence of visited node ids. Return the full list of paths sorted lexicographically.

A single direct edge yields exactly one path `[[0, 1]]`.

Constraints: `2 <= graph.length <= 6` and `0 <= graph[i] <= 5`.

examples.explanation: From node 0 the path forks to 1 and 2, and both rejoin at target 3, giving two lexicographically ordered paths.
The single direct edge is the only path from source to target.
Three routes reach node 4: via 1+3, directly through 3, and the direct edge 0 -> 4; sorted lexicographically the direct edge comes last.

constraints: Inputs are JSON-serializable values satisfying the bounds stated above.
hints: Grow paths forward from node 0, one neighbour at a time.
Keep a single current path: push before recursing and pop when returning.
Copy the path when it reaches the target, then sort all paths lexicographically.

editorial.approach: Backtrack from node 0, extending the current path along each neighbour in order and recording a copy whenever the target is reached. Sort the collected paths lexicographically.
editorial.why_optimal: DFS reuses one path buffer with push and pop instead of copying a prefix for every queue entry, cutting queue memory while enumerating the same paths. On 38 generated cases PAF measured the brute force at 1.40 ms and the optimal at 1.20 ms.
editorial.pitfalls: Record a copy of the path on arrival, not a reference to the live buffer. Sort neighbours during traversal and sort the final list so output order is deterministic.

solutions.title: Brute Force
solutions.complexity: Time: O(2^n * n) | Space: O(2^n * n)

solutions.title: Optimal
solutions.complexity: Time: O(2^n * n) | Space: O(n + P * n)

solutions.code:
def allPathsSourceTarget(graph):
    target = len(graph) - 1
    res = []
    path = [0]
    def dfs(node):
        if node == target:
            res.append(list(path))
            return
        for nxt in sorted(graph[node] if node < len(graph) else []):
            if nxt in path:
                continue
            path.append(nxt)
            dfs(nxt)
            path.pop()
    dfs(0)
    res.sort()
    return res
